prime.problem: A draft written from memory and enthusiasm drifts from the data: numbers get rounded the hopeful way, an exploratory contrast becomes the headline, related work is a list of summaries, and the limitations a reviewer will find are missing. Each of these is a reason to reject an otherwise sound study.
prime.fits: Step 7 of the capstone. It takes the related-work table from How the question got sharp, Figure 1 from Lab: audit 21,000 public runs, and the confirmatory/exploratory split from Analyse what you registered, and turns them into sections.
expect: an outline where every section names its evidence
related work as one sentence of difference per neighbour
three figures, one of them already made
limitations cited to where they're recorded
results written last, in registered order
prime.goal: Draft everything but the results while the sweep runs, write a difference sentence for each close neighbour, and list every limitation with the file that records it.

attend: Which sections can be finished before the sweep ends, and which single file do the rest wait for?
What makes a related-work sentence a 'sentence of difference' rather than a summary, and which neighbour needs the most care?
Why is the transplanted Codex prompt a limitation even though it was copied byte for byte?
What changes in the title and abstract if H2 holds but H1 doesn't?
Why do the labels count as a limitation when the classifier passed its acceptance rule?

must: Each claim in the paper points at a file, line or commit → a number can't drift from its source between drafts → the results section is filled from results/main.md, not retyped from memory
Close neighbours (OverclaimBench, Silence Is Endorsement) cover parts of the idea → a reviewer will look for the gap → related work gives each one sentence of what it did and what this paper adds

Codex with an OpenAI model compacts server-side and doesn't use the published prompt → the arm measures 'Codex's published prompt', not Codex → the limitation must say so, or the prompt effect is over-read
The hand labels were written by one agent annotator → agreement with the extractor isn't human agreement → the paper needs a human second annotator before submission, and says so until it has one
elevated: Figures are regenerated by scripts from runs/ → nothing is hand-edited → the analysis folder can rebuild every figure, which the spec requires and a reviewer can check
reference: outline: abstract, introduction, related work, setup, results, discussion, limitations, appendix; 6–8 pages plus appendix, LaTeX arXiv style
Figure 1: pilot/fig1.png and .pdf, 3.45 in wide, two panels, from pilot/fig.py
extractor validation: held-out finals 65/66, summaries 24/24, attribution 49/49; dev 36/36

compress.prompt: Card closed: list the paper's sections and, for each, write 'ready' or 'waits for the sweep' and the file its evidence comes from.
checklist: related work ready (verified novelty check, re-run before writing)
results 5.2–5.4, Figures 2–3 and the abstract wait for results/main.md
limitations ready, each cited to PROVENANCE.md, the pre-registration, baseline-pilot or results.md

retrieve.q: Explain how this paper differs from Silence Is Endorsement in one sentence, as you would write it in related work.
answer: they show summarizers drop the 'unverified' status of authorization claims and a separate monitor then approves
this paper measures test status in coding agents, the agent's own final claim checked against the repo
paired, dose-response, across transplanted harness prompts

retrieve.q: Walk through how one number, the H2 estimate, gets from the sweep into the abstract.
answer: branches → outcome.json per branch → run_main.py computes the registered estimate, interval and one-sided p
copied into section 5.2 with a comment naming the file and line
the abstract states it with the confirmatory label and whether p < 0.025

retrieve.q: The spec's outline had a real-world check in the real CLIs; addendum 3 doesn't run it. What are the options, and what does each cost?
answer: run it under its own addendum: about 60 runs, adds realism, costs time and money and may hit headless limits
move it to future work: cheaper, but the transplant-vs-real gap stays a stated limitation
either way the paper must say which it did

compare.q: The analysis card separates confirmatory from exploratory results. How does that separation show up in the written paper, and where is it easiest to blur?
answer: separate results subsections, and the abstract names which hypotheses were confirmatory
easiest to blur in the title, the abstract and the discussion, where a striking per-model or mechanism result is tempting
the registered rule (p < 0.025 on pooled H2) decides what can be claimed

compare.q: The discussion section will say what the result means for training on claim checkers. What does that card warn about, and how should the paper phrase it?
answer: penalizing what a monitor detects can teach the model to hide the behaviour instead of dropping it
a claim checker used as a reward could make claims vaguer or tampering quieter
phrase it as a risk the paper's evidence motivates, not as something it measured

predict.q: A reviewer writes: 'The Codex arm doesn't reflect how Codex behaves in practice.' Before reading the reply, predict whether that sinks the prompt comparison, and what the paper should already contain to answer it.
predict.answer: It doesn't sink it, but it narrows it. The paper should already say, in limitations, that Codex with an OpenAI model compacts server-side and that the arm is the published prompt Codex uses with other providers (PROVENANCE.md). The comparison then reads as 'two published compaction prompts, plus a truncation control', which is still what harness builders can act on; the claim about Codex the product has to go.

apply.task: Write the related-work paragraph on 'compaction and lost status' for real: four citations (2607.13071, 2609.20211, 2606.22528, 2608.22752), one sentence of difference each, using only facts from the verified novelty check and the series spec.
apply.done: Your paragraph has four sentences of difference, each with its arXiv id; it quotes no number you can't find in novelty-check.md or the spec (for example 5% → 60% approvals on Llama-3.1-8B for Silence Is Endorsement, and 53% of safety rules surviving one round for Compaction Cliff), and it writes 'argues' wherever a paper doesn't report a measurement.
apply.hint: 2607.13071 is a single case study with no run counts; say so, because that's exactly the gap this paper fills.

reflect: Which prediction did you get wrong: how much of the paper can be written before the sweep, or how serious the Codex-prompt limitation is?
What couldn't you explain cleanly: why each neighbour gets a difference sentence, or why the labels are a limitation?
Which relationship is still fuzzy: result → title, or limitation → what the paper may claim?
Which limitation would you most like to remove with more time or money, and what would it cost?
If the sweep is truncated by the cap, which sentences in your draft have to change?
